clue.text: Trick nurse in debate

parts.note: to con someone is to trick them
to tend is to nurse or look after

explanation.surface: A dodgy ploy to put a nurse into a discussion.
explanation.definitionFit: To contend is to argue a point, a close synonym of debating it.

clue.text: Embrace seal

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a tight hug, as of lovers or boxers
second meaning: to settle or secure a deal

explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a close hug and the act of finally securing an agreement.

clue.text: Peer into US city — almost

indicators.note: the peer's title is placed into the city abbreviation

parts.note: NY is the abbreviation for New York
an earl is a peer of the realm

explanation.surface: A nobleman gazes at an American city, or nearly does.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Peer' looks like a verb meaning to look closely; here it is EARL, which goes 'into' NY.
explanation.definitionFit: Nearly and almost are interchangeable adverbs meaning not quite.

clue.text: Former lover on course with worker going beyond the usual limits

parts.note: an ex is a former partner
an orbit is the course a planet follows
the worker ant is the crossword's usual worker

explanation.surface: An ex-partner heading off with a labourer and overstepping the mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Exorbitant literally means out of the track, so excessive or beyond what is reasonable.

clue.text: Greek letter infidel taxman conceals

indicators.note: the phrase infidel taxman holds the answer within its letters

parts.note: the answer sits across the end of infidel and the start of taxman

explanation.surface: A tax collector who is an unbeliever hides a Greek character.
explanation.definitionFit: Delta is the fourth character of the Greek alphabet.

clue.text: Walk back then jump into retail unit

indicators.note: back tells us to read the word for walk from right to left

parts.note: to step is to walk
a hop is a small jump

explanation.surface: Retracing your steps and leaping into a shop.
explanation.definitionFit: A pet shop is a store that sells animals and their supplies, so a kind of retail unit.

clue.text: One travelling quietly with idiot, engineer and old Queen

parts.note: P is piano, the musical term for quiet
an ass is an idiot, and ENG is the usual short form of engineer
ER, Elizabeth Regina, the late Queen

explanation.surface: A traveller with a fool, an engineer and a former monarch for company.
explanation.definitionFit: A passenger is someone carried on a journey in a vehicle without driving it.

clue.text: Food from lorry missing second element

indicators.note: missing means the named letter is dropped from the vehicle word

parts.note: a truck is a lorry
R is the second letter of truck

explanation.surface: Something to eat from a lorry lacking a chemical part.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Second element' sounds like chemistry, but it is R, the second letter of TRUCK, which goes 'missing'. Tuck is British school slang for snacks.
explanation.definitionFit: Tuck is informal British slang for food, especially sweets and snacks eaten at school.

clue.text: Run off after domestic pest

indicators.note: after puts the running-off word behind the household word

parts.note: domestic means relating to the house
to fly is to flee or run off

explanation.surface: Something bolting after a household nuisance.
explanation.definitionFit: The common housefly is an insect regarded as a nuisance and disease carrier indoors.

clue.text: Rule out putting contralto in overture

indicators.note: the voice abbreviation goes in the word for an opening piece

parts.note: a prelude is an introductory piece, an overture

explanation.surface: Banning a contralto from singing in the opening number.
explanation.definitionFit: To preclude something is to prevent it or make it impossible in advance.

clue.text: One possessed flipping love for state

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: flipping turns the word for possessed back to front

parts.note: had means possessed
love is zero in tennis, shaped like O

explanation.surface: Someone besotted flipping out over love in a particular state.
explanation.definitionFit: Idaho is one of the fifty states of the USA, in the north-west.

clue.text: Mislaid reason for hopeless endeavour

parts.note: lost means mislaid
a cause is a reason

explanation.surface: Losing your rationale for a doomed effort.
explanation.definitionFit: A lost cause is an idiom for an aim or effort that has no chance of success.

clue.text: Feted rebel acted out

indicators.note: out signals the letters of rebel acted are put into a new order

explanation.surface: An honoured rebel performed a part on stage.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone feted is honoured and praised publicly, which is what being celebrated means.

clue.text: Endlessly touches fish

indicators.note: endlessly means both the first and last letters are removed

parts.note: feels means touches

explanation.surface: Constantly fingering a fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Endlessly' looks like an adverb meaning constantly; here it strips both ends of FEELS.
explanation.definitionFit: The eel is a long snake-like species of fish.

clue.text: Savage crossing hill and winning

indicators.note: the word for savage spans across the hill word, holding it inside

parts.note: vicious means savage
a tor is a rocky hill, as on Dartmoor

explanation.surface: A wild beast traversing a hill and coming out on top.
explanation.definitionFit: Victorious means having won, so it fits winning as an adjective.

clue.text: Resolute way Ron grimaced at first then left

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for street, a way

indicators.note: at first takes only the opening letter of grimaced

parts.note: G is the first letter of grimaced
willed means left in a will, bequeathed

explanation.surface: Ron pulls a face and then departs in a determined manner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'At first' takes just the G of grimaced. 'Left' is not departed but bequeathed by will.
explanation.definitionFit: A strong-willed person is determined and not easily swayed, so resolute.

clue.text: Artist welcomed by poorest miserable machinists

indicators.note: the artist abbreviation is taken in by the word poorest
miserable suggests something in a wretched state, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, an artist

explanation.surface: A painter is greeted by the poorest, unhappy factory workers.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram comes first and the container second: the shuffled letters of the poorest take in the Academician.
explanation.definitionFit: Operators are people who run machines, so machinists by another name.

clue.text: Warn in notice — day is hot

parts.note: an ad is a notice, an advertisement
MON is the abbreviation for Monday
H is the abbreviation for hot on taps

explanation.surface: A public notice cautions that the day will be sweltering.
explanation.definitionFit: To admonish someone is to caution or reprove them firmly.

clue.text: Upsetting details about duck being detached

indicators.note: about means the letters of details are placed around the duck letter
upsetting suggests knocking things over, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: a duck is a score of zero in cricket, written O

explanation.surface: Distressing particulars about a duck being cut loose.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram comes first and the container second: the shuffled details go round the cricketer's zero.
explanation.definitionFit: Isolated means separated from others, so cut off or detached.

clue.text: Strangely design attire to fall apart

indicators.note: strangely signals the letters of design attire take an odd new order

explanation.surface: Outlandish clothes designed to come apart.
explanation.definitionFit: To disintegrate is to break up into small pieces, so to collapse or fall apart.

clue.text: Cause harm to barrier over time

indicators.note: in a down clue over puts the barrier word above the time word

parts.note: a dam is a barrier across water
an age is a long period of time

explanation.surface: Hurting a dam over the course of the years.
explanation.definitionFit: To damage something is to injure or harm it.

clue.text: Hunted and restrained we hear

indicators.note: we hear tells us the answer sounds like the word for restrained

parts.note: chaste means restrained or pure

explanation.surface: Pursued and held back, by all accounts.
explanation.definitionFit: Chased means pursued, as hunters pursue their quarry.

clue.text: Bird not following predator

indicators.note: not means the abbreviation for following is left out

parts.note: a fowl is a bird
F is the abbreviation for following, as in page references

explanation.surface: A bird that does not go after a predator.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bird' looks like the definition, but it is FOWL; 'not' following, F, leaves the definition 'predator'.
explanation.definitionFit: The owl is a nocturnal bird of prey, a hunter of mice and small animals.

clue.text: Rubbish black tree and dead tree

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils
the alder is a tree
the ash is a tree

explanation.surface: Talk of a blackened tree and a dead tree is nonsense.
explanation.definitionFit: Balderdash is senseless talk, synonymous with nonsense or rubbish.

clue.text: Force dropping uniform clothing

indicators.note: dropping means the uniform letter is let go from the word for force

parts.note: duress is force or compulsion
U is uniform in the NATO alphabet

explanation.surface: Coercion to abandon uniformed attire.
explanation.walkthrough: DURESS is 'dropping' U; 'uniform' seems to belong with clothing but just gives that letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Dress means clothes in general, as in evening dress.

clue.text: Group of players principally taking roles in operetta

indicators.note: principally means taking the leading letter of each of the following words

parts.note: the opening letters of taking, roles, in and operetta

explanation.surface: Musicians mostly playing parts in a light opera.
explanation.definitionFit: A trio is a set of three musicians performing together.

clue.text: Bury Post Office initially send everything to place inbetween

parts.note: to inter is to bury

indicators.note: initially takes the opening letter of each of send and everything

parts.note: S and E, the first letters of send and everything

explanation.surface: A town's post office sending all its mail to some halfway spot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Initially' takes SE from send and everything. Bury is also a town near Manchester, which the surface plays on.
explanation.definitionFit: To interpose is to insert or put something between other things.

clue.text: Duck hit revolving stones

parts.note: a duck is zero in cricket, written O

indicators.note: revolving turns the word for hit round so it reads backwards

parts.note: to slap is to hit

explanation.surface: Ducking a blow from spinning rocks.
explanation.definitionFit: Opals are iridescent gemstones, the precious stones of the definition.

clue.text: Revolting rogue regularly wearing animal skins

indicators.note: the skins are worn around the letters picked from rogue

parts.note: hides are animal skins

indicators.note: regularly takes every other letter of rogue, here the second and fourth

parts.note: the second and fourth letters of rogue are O and U

explanation.surface: A disgusting scoundrel dressed in furs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Regularly' takes OU from rogue, and 'wearing' has the skins wrapped around those letters, as clothes go round a body.
explanation.definitionFit: Hideous means very ugly or repulsive, as revolting does.

clue.text: Hold up pay out across America

indicators.note: the spending word stretches across the country abbreviation, holding it within

parts.note: to spend is to pay out money
US is the abbreviation for the United States

explanation.surface: A delayed payment travelling across America.
explanation.definitionFit: To suspend something is to hang it up or to halt it temporarily.
